cells.tense: You are settling what is finished and pointing the rest somewhere.
cells.ask: Walk through one room and take out one thing that already served its purpose; clear the spot before you decide what goes there next.
cells.core:
You're at a clear edge with this. Something in your life has finished — not failed, finished — and you're letting it end instead of dragging it forward. You can also point. When the question is which way to go next, you know, and you don't need to argue it to anyone.

The two together are rarer than either alone. You're clearing and choosing at once, and neither is frantic. Let someone nearby be part of it if they're free. What you're holding, you're holding without squeezing. That doesn't need defending. It needs to keep going at the pace it's already going.

cells.tense: You are trying to write the ending before it has decided to write itself.
cells.ask: Pick an ending that is actually underway and today make one decision about it you can live with this week, then leave it alone until it moves.
cells.core:
You're already living past the thing, deciding what it will mean, choosing the story before the ending has happened. The ending isn't yours to schedule. Run ahead of it and you skip the stretch where it closes on its own — and that stretch is what would let a new direction actually hold.

Stand at one ending that's underway. Let it finish in its own time. The pull is strong, and the force you're putting into it is bending what could be a clean cut. Stop pushing and something truer might get to speak. Until then, you won't know which direction is yours and which is the one you picked while bracing. One decision today, then hands off.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you and did not open again.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you've been tending past its usefulness — a habit, an object, a commitment to someone — and today take one small step to release it.
cells.core:
There's a direction that was yours, and you're not picking it up. It isn't inspiration that's missing. Something ended, and you're still in the room with the door shut behind you, facing the wrong way. That happens. What matters more than the ending is turning around.

A direction to steer by stays out of reach while an old one is still running the tab. What's already cleared in your life is asking for a next step, and it keeps not getting one. Start where the clearing actually is — a person, a commitment, a habit you've been carrying because putting it down felt like a bigger move than you could make. Small counts.

cells.tense: You are pointing the way and calling it just how things worked out.
cells.ask: Tell one person something you've decided to head toward, and how you decided, before you run through the reasons why it makes sense.
cells.core:
You've already chosen a direction — probably a few — and you keep presenting them as things that happened. The picture of what's next, the way you clear a room, the timing of the ending: yours. Watch what you call the situation and what you call your decision. Nothing is wrong with the choice. What's off is whose it says it is.

No one is asking you to defend it. A person who sees this about you could simply be told — not asked to agree, just told. Say it as yours and the direction gets clearer, and the ending stops holding the room. Not a claim about who you are. A claim about whose decision this is. Yours already.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person has a genuine sense of direction to end or clear — the record gives the card as a capacity, not as evidence of present direction, and the seat says endings are pending, not that any particular ending exists. Reader's objection: 'there's no direction here to speak of, and nothing is ending' — so each cell is narrowed toward the sorting that happens when something ends or is cleared, and the ending named is one they would pick, not one I assert. The ask stays useful if wrong: each motion is something they can do in a day and learn from even if my read misses; the sentence that serves the writer is the one that hands over the recognition, and it is the one I cut.

Reader's objection: 'nothing is ending for me' — the asks survive that, since clearing one finished thing and choosing a direction are doable either way and teach the same sorting. The sentence that serves me more than them was a tidy closing beat about holding the weight while steering; the closing move is different in each cell now, and none of them praises the person for what I invented.
